concerns.text: FR-003 and SC-001 mandate discarding the bottom [deferred] (a percentile-based distribution rule). T007b and T016 replace this with a hardcoded absolute score threshold (60.0) and explicitly forbid dynamic percentile calculation. This is a semantic weakening of the experimental design, converting a distributional hypothesis into a fixed-value rule not present in the spec.

FR-002 requires a 'lightweight' CPU-based physics filter. T015b and T018b implement 'Video-to-Simulation Reconstruction' using optical flow and object detection. This introduces a heavy Computer Vision dependency not authorized by the spec's 'lightweight' constraint and contradicts the plan's assertion of using only 'standard CPU-tractable libraries' without CV stacks.

FR-005 and SC-003 require evaluating against the PhysisForcing baseline. T033a-1 mandates fetching these results from an external source (paper/repo) with a hard abort on failure. The spec assumes the baseline is available for comparison; the task introduces a fragile external dependency with no fallback strategy, risking the inability to measure SC-003 (comparability) if the fetch fails.

SC-005 requires measuring training time against a 'predefined time limit' (constraint). T025 hardcodes the limit to 'maximum 3 epochs' to guarantee completion. This conflates the *result* (duration) with the *constraint* (time limit), preventing independent verification of whether the model meets the time limit under varying loads, as the task dictates the duration rather than measuring it.

FR-009 mandates augmentation only if retained count < 30. T034 samples from the 'augmented curated dataset' for evaluation. If augmentation was triggered, the evaluation set is artificially inflated, potentially violating the statistical power assumptions of the TOST test (FR-006) which assumes natural data distribution, not augmented samples.
